title: Serbia's Student Movement Unveils Election Victory Amid Protests
summary: A student-led movement in Serbia aims to oust the ruling party of veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic by participating in a key parliamentary vote on Sunday, with over 150,000 supporters gathering in central Belgrade. The movement seeks to end more than 14 years of Vucic’s rightwing populist rule.

facts.statement: A student-led movement in Serbia aims to oust the ruling party of veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic by participating in a key parliamentary vote on Sunday.
Over 150,000 supporters gathered in central Belgrade to support the movement.
The movement seeks to end more than 14 years of Vucic’s rightwing populist rule.

sources.description:
State paid consultancy firm $166,000 for feasibility study on merging the three tertiary institutions

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Western Australian government has said it is “extremely disappointed” and is seeking an “expedited” cost recovery from Deloitte after errors were discovered in a report about a potential university merger, including AI-hallucinated references and hundreds of millions of dollars in cost discrepancies.

The government paid Deloitte $166,000 for a feasibility study on merging the University of Western Australia, Curtin University and Murdoch University.

sources.title: Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić ousted by student movement in seismic election
sources.description:
Vučić’s 12-year reign looks to have been ended by record turnout of voters in election provoked by student-led protests

The long-serving leader of Serbia, Aleksandar Vučić, has conceded defeat, ushering in a seismic political shift after a historic election that saw ​the increasingly authoritarian leader pitted against a student-led movement that had spent two years protesting against his government.

Vučić pointed to preliminary results that suggested voters had overwhelmingly backed the students, potentially giving them a majority in the country’s 250-seat parliament.

sources.title: Serbia election: Vucic faces tough challenge from student-backed movement
sources.description:
Serbians are voting Sunday in a parliamentary election that is seen as a showdown between the Balkan country's populist leader Aleksandar Vucic and a movement of university students who led protests against him for almost two years.
Though Serbia's 6.4 million voters get to choose from 18 parties hoping to enter the 250-member Parliament, the election has taken shaped as a referendum between Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party and the youth-backed Students' List.
The main contenders are believed to be polling neck-and-neck, making Sunday's election the most uncertain in recent years. Turnout is expected to be high and could push most smaller parties below the 3% threshold needed to make it into the assembly.
While Vucic has routinely outplayed Serbia's fractured opposition in the past, the leaderless youth movement has proved to be a tough opponent that rattled his firm grip on power in Serbia like no one else could in the past 14 years since his party took office.
